description:
Num pontinho azul pálido, três pessoas olharam para cima e decidiram ir além. Somos a Capella Stars, nome de uma estrela que parece uma luz só, mas são quatro sóis. Somos feitos de poeira de estrelas e viemos transformar curiosidade em algo real.

On a pale blue dot, three people looked up and chose to go further. We are Capella Stars, named after a star that looks like one light but is really four suns. Made of star-stuff, we came to turn curiosity into something real. Per aspera ad astra.
summary:
Cosmos Odyssey is an interactive, browser-based educational game that transforms space mission design into an engaging learning experience. Inspired by NASA's seven-phase mission lifecycle, the game allows players to take on the role of a space engineering team, making critical decisions throughout the development of a scientific mission, from initial planning and spacecraft design to launch, operations, and mission completion.

Players must balance resources, select spacecraft components, solve unexpected challenges, and understand how engineering decisions affect mission success. By incorporating concepts and examples from real NASA missions, Cosmos Odyssey bridges the gap between complex aerospace engineering principles and accessible education.

Our project aims to make space exploration more understandable and engaging, inspiring students to develop scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and an interest in STEM fields.
details:
How Does It Work?

Cosmos Odyssey is an interactive educational game that simulates the complete lifecycle of a scientific space mission, following NASA's seven project phases, from Pre-Phase A to Phase F.

The player takes on the role of a space engineering team and progresses through seven interconnected stages:

  1. Concept Studies: Compare three mission alternatives inspired by real space missions.
  2. Concept Development: Select the mission objective, choose a launch facility (Kennedy, Vandenberg, or Wallops), and explore launch opportunities.
  3. Preliminary Design: Build a spacecraft by selecting components for five engineering disciplines: power, propulsion, thermal control, communications, and scientific payload.
  4. Final Design and Fabrication: Assemble a rocket using a drag-and-drop system and adjust its parameters within manufacturing tolerances.
  5. Assembly, Integration, and Testing: Perform a test flight and verify mission requirements. Failed tests may force players to revisit earlier design decisions.
  6. Operations: Launch the spacecraft, manage its journey, and solve unexpected crew challenges through interactive mini-games.
  7. Closeout and Return: Manage atmospheric reentry, parachute deployment, and landing before receiving a final mission performance report.

Every decision has consequences. Science points serve as the mission budget, while fuel consumption, energy, spacecraft mass, and schedule change according to the selected components and engineering decisions. At the end, players receive a report explaining their results, identifying lessons learned, and comparing their spacecraft with real space missions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The main benefit of Cosmos Odyssey is its learning-by-doing approach. Instead of simply reading about aerospace engineering, students actively experience the challenges involved in designing and operating a spacecraft.

The game encourages systems thinking by showing how different engineering disciplines depend on one another. It also develops critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and decision-making skills.

By connecting gameplay to real NASA missions and scientific concepts, Cosmos Odyssey helps make complex aerospace knowledge more accessible to beginners. Our intended impact is to stimulate scientific curiosity, strengthen STEM education, and inspire more students to explore careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.

The project is free, bilingual (English and Portuguese), browser-based, and requires no installation or user registration.

Technology and Development Tools

The entire game was developed using HTML5, CSS, and pure JavaScript, with Canvas 2D for rendering its interactive scenes, spacecraft, rockets, diagrams, and visual elements.

The game is contained in a single index.html file, without external programming frameworks or a backend server. It is hosted on GitHub Pages and uses Google Fonts for typography.

Claude (Anthropic) assisted with programming, content development, and testing, while Google Gemini and Claude supported the research process. AI-generated images were used for the fictional crew caricatures. All other visual scenes were created programmatically using Canvas 2D.

Basic accessibility features include keyboard navigation, reduced-motion support, and status messages for screen readers. The game does not require specialized hardware, collect personal information, or use tracking cookies.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative aspect of Cosmos Odyssey lies in transforming NASA's real mission-development methodology into a continuous, interactive experience. Rather than teaching isolated facts about rockets or planets, the game demonstrates how an entire space mission works as an interconnected system.

Its main design principle is that engineering decisions involve trade-offs: every choice offers advantages and disadvantages, and there is no universally perfect spacecraft. Players must balance competing requirements and understand how early decisions influence the final outcome.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, educational accessibility, gameplay balance, technical feasibility, and the need to simplify complex engineering concepts without losing their meaning.

We also prioritized accessibility and privacy by making the game free, bilingual, browser-based, and independent of user accounts.

Cosmos Odyssey was designed to turn the complexity of space exploration into an experience that students can understand, experiment with, and enjoy.
